advantages.what: A missing, non-string or empty FEN gets a plain Error 'Invalid FEN: expected a string' instead of an internal TypeError
The suite tests invalid FENs (13 malformed inputs across all three functions, asserting an Invalid FEN error), so the validation contract is guarded; Y has no invalid-FEN test
The suite times the middlegame and depth-2 limits (a slowdown fails TC-8); in Y a 2.1 s depth-2 count still passes npm test
README tells the caller about FEN validation and impossible positions, the error class, and how inconsistent castling or en-passant fields are treated
README tells the caller that a saved FEN resumes or branches play in a fresh process
No builder acceptance harness shipped beside the product (Y ships acceptance/*.cjs not run by npm test), and no tests pinning conversion-hook call counts

lesser_lacks: Check the FEN is a non-empty string up front and throw a descriptive invalid-FEN error
Add tests that pass malformed FENs to legalMoves, status and applyMove and assert the thrown error
Add a test that times legalMoves on a middlegame position and the depth-2 start count against the stated limits
Document FEN validation, impossible-position handling, the IllegalMoveError shape and castling/en-passant field handling in the README
Remove or explain the acceptance/ directory
pairs.why: Both engines are correct on every stated requirement and every perft count; Z adds a clean error for non-string FENs, guards its FEN validation and its two speed limits with tests, and documents more of its behaviour. Y's only edge is a README line on resuming from a saved FEN, and it carries a shipped acceptance harness. The gap is a small, well-defined follow-up.

A missing, non-string or empty FEN gets a descriptive error instead of an internal TypeError
The suite tests invalid FENs and asserts the error; X has no invalid-FEN test
README documents FEN validation, impossible positions, move-string strictness, the error class and inconsistent castling/en-passant fields; X tells none of these

lesser_lacks: Validate FEN syntax (string type, eight ranks of eight squares, known piece letters, side, castling, en-passant and clock fields) and throw a descriptive invalid-FEN error from all three functions
Add tests passing malformed FENs to legalMoves, status and applyMove asserting that error
Document in the README the FEN validation, impossible-position tolerance, move-string strictness and the IllegalMoveError shape
pairs.why: The engines, test coverage of the named subjects and timing guards are equivalent, and every perft count matches in both. X has no FEN validation, so malformed input gets confident wrong answers (D-1) or raw TypeErrors (D-2), with nothing documented and no test for that path. Adding a validating parser, its tests and README lines is about an hour of work.

README documents the move-string contract and resuming or branching from a saved FEN
The suite times both speed limits, so a performance regression fails npm test; Y has no timing test
No builder acceptance harness shipped and no tests pinning conversion-hook behaviour a correct product need not share

lesser_lacks: Validate FEN syntax and throw descriptive errors for malformed FENs from all three functions

pairs.why: Both engines are correct on all stated requirements and perft counts, and both leave non-string FENs to an internal TypeError (D-2). Y validates malformed FENs and documents its contract, which matters to whoever runs it; X's edge is a timing test and a cleaner shipped tree, which matter to a maintainer but less. X closes the gap by adding a validating parser and README lines.
